speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing hand tremors and recent memory issues; to better understand your condition, could you please describe how long these symptoms have been occurring and if they are present at rest or only during movement?

speaker: Patient
text: 70-year-old man accompanied by his wife. The patient first noticed the tremor in his left hand 1 year ago, which has been progressively worsening. Recently, he has faced difficulty in performing tasks that require steadiness, such as reading. His wife has observed a decline in his memory, taking note of his forgetfulness in paying bills, a task she has since had to assume.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The tremor has been present for one year, progressing from the left hand to affecting tasks like reading, and your wife notes memory issues with finances. Are these hand tremors more noticeable when your hands are resting on your lap, or do they appear only when you try to perform a specific action?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Resting tremor worse on the left hand. I also have Soft speech, Reduced facial expressions, Memory decline, Difficulty in managing finances.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Parkinson's Disease. The combination of a unilateral resting tremor, soft speech (hypophonia), reduced facial expressions (masked facies), and executive dysfunction (difficulty managing finances) is highly characteristic of idiopathic Parkinson's disease. Given the presence of cognitive decline, I will monitor for progression to Parkinson's Disease Dementia.
